parts.label: b_i
parts.description: Write log_a(a^2 b) in terms of log_a(b)
parts.notes: A1 for 2 + log_a(b). Splits as log_a(a^2) + log_a(b).

parts.label: b_ii
parts.description: Write log_a(b/a) in terms of log_a(b)
parts.notes: A1 for log_a(b) - 1. Splits as log_a(b) - log_a(a).

parts.label: b_iii
parts.description: Write log_a(sqrt(a b^3)) in terms of log_a(b)
parts.tolerance: Accept (1 + 3 log_a(b))/2 or any algebraically equivalent form.
parts.notes: M1 for using power and product laws to reach (1/2)(1 + 3 log_a(b)) or equivalent. A1 for 1/2 + (3/2) log_a(b).

parts.label: b_iv
parts.description: Write log_(a^2)(b) in terms of log_a(b)
parts.notes: M1 for change of base log_(a^2)(b) = log_a(b)/log_a(a^2) = log_a(b)/2. A1 for (1/2) log_a(b).

parts.label: a
parts.description: Sketch y = 2^x on the provided axes; label y-intercept and HA

expected.answer: increasing exponential through (0,1) approaching y=0 from above

parts.tolerance: Accept any clearly-increasing exponential that passes through (0,1) and stays above y=0 with the asymptote indicated.
parts.notes: A1 for correct shape (passes through (0,1), strictly increasing, concave up). A1 for labelling the y-intercept (0,1) AND the horizontal asymptote y=0.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Sketch y = log_2(x); label x-intercept and VA

expected.answer: increasing log curve through (1,0), VA at x=0

parts.tolerance: Sketch should be the reflection of (a) across y=x. Accept curves that pass through (1,0), (2,1), (4,2).
parts.notes: A1 for correct shape (passes through (1,0), increasing, concave down). A1 for labelling the x-intercept (1,0) AND the vertical asymptote x=0.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Domain and range of y=2^x and y=log_2(x)
parts.tolerance: Accept any clear notation for 'all real numbers' (R, (-inf, inf), 'all reals'). For y > 0 accept (0, inf) or 'positive reals'.
parts.notes: A1 per cell, four cells total. Independent A1's — award each cell that is correct.

parts.label: d
parts.description: State point on y=log_2(x) corresponding to (3,8) on y=2^x
parts.notes: A1 for (8, 3). Coordinates swap under reflection across y=x.

source: original (transformations of log_2 x: shift, shift, reflection)

parts.description: Sketch g(x)=log_2(x-2); state VA
parts.notes: A1 for correct sketch shape (parent shifted right 2, passes through (3,0) and (4,1)). A1 for VA x = 2.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Sketch h(x)=log_2(x)+3; state VA
parts.notes: A1 for correct sketch shape (parent shifted up 3). A1 for VA x = 0 (unchanged by vertical shift).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Sketch k(x)=-log_2(x); state VA
parts.notes: A1 for correct sketch shape (parent reflected across x-axis; decreasing, concave up). A1 for VA x = 0 (unchanged by reflection across x-axis).

parts.label: d
parts.description: x-intercept of g(x)=log_2(x-2)

parts.notes: A1 for a = 2^(1/4) (or equivalent exact form). A1 for marking the corresponding point on the graph of f.

parts.notes: A1 for (1, 0). True for any log_b(x): the x-intercept is always (1, 0).

parts.label: a
parts.description: h from VA x=2 in y=log_3(x-h)+k
parts.notes: A1 for h = 2. VA of log_b(x-h)+k is x = h.

parts.label: b
parts.description: k given the curve passes through (5, 4)
parts.notes: M1 for substituting (5,4) into y = log_3(x-2) + k to get 4 = log_3(3) + k. A1 for k = 3.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Sketch y = log_3(x-2) + 3 with VA and the point (5,4)

expected.answer: VA at x=2; curve passes through (3,3), (5,4), (11,5)

parts.tolerance: Sketch should pass through (3,3) and (5,4); VA drawn explicitly.
parts.notes: A1 for VA drawn at x=2 (e.g. dashed vertical line). A1 for correct shape (parent log_3 shape, shifted right 2 and up 3; passes through (3,3) and (5,4)). A1 for the point (5,4) marked on the curve.
parts.follow_through: Award all three sketch marks based on the candidate's h and k from (a) and (b), even if those values are wrong.
